content: Docusate is an over-the-counter (OTC) laxative approved by the FDA for the treatment of constipation. It is primarily used to relieve occasional constipation caused by hard stools. The effects on stool softening are typically observed within 1 to 3 days after the initial dose. Dosage and Administration: Adults and children aged 12 years and older: The oral dosage is 5 to 20 mL (1 to 4 teaspoonfuls) once daily or as directed by a physician. Children aged 6 to under 12 years: The oral dosage is 5 to 10 mL (1 to 2 teaspoonfuls) once daily or as directed by a physician. Children under 3 years of age: Consult a physician for appropriate dosing. Higher doses are recommended for initial therapy, and the dosage should be adjusted based on individual response. To mask the bitter taste, the product may be mixed with 6 to 8 ounces of milk, fruit juice, or infant formula. Contraindications and Warnings: Do not use laxative products if abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting are present unless directed by a physician. Avoid using this product for more than one week unless under medical supervision. If there is a sudden change in bowel habits persisting for more than two weeks, consult a physician before using a laxative. Rectal bleeding or failure to have a bowel movement after using a laxative may indicate a serious condition. Discontinue use and seek medical advice. Pregnant or nursing individuals should consult a healthcare professional before using this product. Keep this and all medications out of the reach of children. In case of accidental overdose, seek immediate medical assistance or contact a Poison Control Center. Adverse Reactions: Common side effects include stomach pain, diarrhea, or cramping. There is limited information available regarding post-marketing adverse reactions. Drug Interactions: Do not take this product if you are currently using mineral oil or a prescription drug unless directed by a physician. Use in Specific Populations: There is no FDA guidance on the use of Docusate in pregnant or nursing mothers, pediatric patients, geriatric patients, or specific gender or racial populations. There is also no FDA guidance on its use in patients with renal or hepatic impairment, immunocompromised patients, or individuals of reproductive potential. Pharmacology: Each 5 mL (teaspoonful) contains 50 mg of docusate sodium. Other ingredients include citric acid, D&C Red No. 33, flavoring, glycerin, propylene glycol, purified water, sodium citrate, sodium saccharin, and sorbitol. The sodium content is 14 mg per 5 mL. There is limited information available regarding the mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology of Docusate. Storage: Store the product tightly closed at controlled room temperature (20°C to 25°C or 68°F to 77°F). Protect it from freezing and light. Precautions with Alcohol: The interaction between alcohol and Docusate has not been established. Consult your doctor regarding the effects of alcohol consumption while taking this medication. Brand Names: Docusate Sodium® is a common brand name for this medication. Additional Notes: There is limited information available regarding off-label uses, clinical studies, IV compatibility, and patient counseling information for Docusate.
